touches.text: The shims, each connected to the bus, pick up the messages and route them to their device in whatever manner is appropriate.
Trouble Ticket: an error that needs a non-automated fixer (CC or Akien).

The intention for a trouble ticket is that it is a diagnostic report. EXACTLY like the Trouble Tickets in the Number Five Crossbar Telephone Switch. It MUST include EVERYTHING needed to diagnose, isolate, and repair the trouble.
In the event a second trouble is observed while the first is open, a new ticket is NEVER issued, we just increment a counter on the ticket.
Trouble Tickets are disposable artifacts once closed. They are file artifacts, live in the logging tree, and are cleared out on a 30 day cycle by the cairn device during a sleep cycle.
They show on the operator's to-do list (8.2.6).
Trouble: it has to be able to report when nothing else can, so direct lines to trouble make sense for recovery reasons (7.3.4).
Trouble tickets (3.3.3) live here. Any device has a direct line to raise one, not over the bus (2.2.8.1.3).
This device's web panel is the operator's to do list...
TESTER MACHINE, CodeMother's (was the tester device, cairn/devices/tester/)
Runs a proof as its own process and writes a validation record (claim, caller, date, method, verdict, evidence, falsifier, horizon).
